## 操作环境
Linux普通用户UID1000，平台已校验的RPM4.18.2、dpkg、GnuPG及原生exec观察工具。仅自建私有db/root/prefix；禁止系统安装、服务、镜像、部署和默认身份/PATH变化。缺工具则环境未就绪，不用模拟代替。

## 操作任务
完成package.spec，真实构建opsforge-demo 1.0和2.0数据包，保持Source0、原生BuildRequires/Requires、prep/build/install/check/files分工、隔离buildroot和含空格文件清单。平台提供的私有工具与构建/运行依赖分别实际验证。签名验真并拒绝篡改；实际私有安装、升级、回退及卸载验证配置与业务状态保留。不得添加维护脚本、读取主机秘密或写系统根。交付packaging-notes.md解释原题知识点、原始命令与证据边界。 原生分别执行-bp/-bc/-bi：prep解包但不安装，build验证构建输入但不向buildroot放payload，只有install写入buildroot；用实际文件与随机源内容证明阶段边界。

## 产物
- package.spec
- packaging-notes.md

## 验收方法
原生工具实际消费交付文件；核原始命令、退出码、随机payload、包元数据与状态。正解、合法替代须通过；未完成、不同错解、投机和early-exit须拒绝。语义说明另由非作者审阅，不以关键词打分。

# Native package scope and evidence
These fixtures are data-only packages in private RPM databases/prefixes and a private dpkg root. No host package installation, service, image, deployment or cloud resource is involved. The native command journal is the evidence; the text alone cannot demonstrate a successful operation.

RPM header metadata records Name/Version/Release/Summary/License/Architecture, file ownership and dependency information; the archive payload is distinct from that header. Source0 identifies the archive; BuildRequires is checked at build time, while Requires is checked at install time. A data-only fixture has AutoReqProv disabled and declares its explicit teaching dependencies; this is not a general recommendation to disable automatic dependency discovery for real programs. Prep unpacks source, build verifies the actual build input, install stages into buildroot, check tests that staged source is usable, files enumerates the payload. Buildroot is never the running system root.

The reference actually produces two versions. Native RPM header, requirements, files and empty script metadata are queried. A disposable local RSA key signs the RPM; rpmkeys verifies the trusted key, and altered bytes fail. An unsigned RPM can pass digest checking without being authenticated, so `digests OK` alone is rejected as proof of signature. The build and runtime dependency failure paths are deliberately exercised. No `--nodeps` is used to suppress them.

RPM %config(noreplace) preserves administrator edits during upgrade and creates .rpmnew; erasure preserves a modified config as .rpmsave. Debian control declares Depends, conffiles declares persistent configuration, and --force-confold makes the noninteractive preservation choice explicit; the alternative version appears as .dpkg-dist. A failed dpkg install can leave an unpacked package: dependency failure is not an atomic rollback. Removal preserves conffiles; purge removes managed config. User state outside the package file list survives upgrade, rollback and removal. The teaching fixture keeps the same data format in both versions; a real incompatible data migration needs a separate compatibility plan.

A .deb is not intrinsically authenticated by a package checksum. The fixture uses a detached GPG signature over the exact package bytes and verifies that signature with an explicit private public-key ring. Normal Debian repository authentication uses signed repository metadata; this local detached-signature exercise does not claim to implement an APT repository. No maintainer scripts are needed here; if present they require separate review and a confined runtime. Never install an unknown package merely to inspect its contents, and never read host secrets from a build or installation hook.

Rollback here is a native downgrade to the exact earlier package in the same private root, followed by file/config/state checks. It is not a production rollback claim. All disposable package databases, roots, keys, agents and files are removed by the validation harness. Real signing identity, repository trust and production rollout remain outside this exercise.

Priority: optional

   self.source(version);p,file=self.build(spec,'opsforge-demo',version);assert p.returncode==0 and file,p.stdout+p.stderr
   meta=self.rpm('-qp','--queryformat','%{NAME}|%{VERSION}|%{RELEASE}|%{ARCH}|%{LICENSE}',file).stdout;assert meta=='opsforge-demo|'+version+'|1|noarch|MIT','wrong native RPM header'
   assert 'opsforge-runtime-data' in self.rpm('-qp','--requires',file).stdout,'runtime dependency missing'
   files=self.rpm('-qpl',file).stdout.splitlines();assert '/opt/opsforge-demo/data with spaces.txt' in files and '/opt/opsforge-demo/settings.conf' in files
   assert not self.rpm('-qp','--scripts',file).stdout.strip(),'data-only exercise forbids installation hooks';self.sign_rpm(file);made.append(file)
  p=self.rpm('--prefix',self.prefix,'-i',made[0],ok=False);assert p.returncode!=0 and 'opsforge-runtime-data' in p.stderr
  self.rpm('--prefix',self.prefix,'-i',runtime);self.rpm('--prefix',self.prefix,'-i',made[0]);assert self.nonce in (self.prefix/'data with spaces.txt').read_text()
  state=self.prefix/'state/data.txt';state.parent.mkdir();state.write_text('preserve-user-data-'+self.nonce);conf=self.prefix/'settings.conf';conf.write_text('mode=operator\n')
  self.rpm('--prefix',self.prefix,'-U',made[1]);assert conf.read_text()=='mode=operator\n','RPM upgrade overwrote administrator config';assert '2.0' in (self.prefix/'data with spaces.txt').read_text();assert (self.prefix/'settings.conf.rpmnew').exists()
  self.rpm('--prefix',self.prefix,'--oldpackage','-U',made[0]);assert '1.0' in (self.prefix/'data with spaces.txt').read_text() and conf.read_text()=='mode=operator\n';self.rpm('-ql','opsforge-demo');self.rpm('-e','opsforge-demo')
  assert not (self.prefix/'data with spaces.txt').exists();assert (self.prefix/'settings.conf.rpmsave').read_text()=='mode=operator\n';assert state.read_text()=='preserve-user-data-'+self.nonce

# Native package scope and evidence
These fixtures are data-only packages in private RPM databases/prefixes and a private dpkg root. No host package installation, service, image, deployment or cloud resource is involved. The native command journal is the evidence; the text alone cannot demonstrate a successful operation.

RPM header metadata records Name/Version/Release/Summary/License/Architecture, file ownership and dependency information; the archive payload is distinct from that header. Source0 identifies the archive; BuildRequires is checked at build time, while Requires is checked at install time. A data-only fixture has AutoReqProv disabled and declares its explicit teaching dependencies; this is not a general recommendation to disable automatic dependency discovery for real programs. Prep unpacks source, build verifies the actual build input, install stages into buildroot, check tests that staged source is usable, files enumerates the payload. Buildroot is never the running system root.

The reference actually produces two versions. Native RPM header, requirements, files and empty script metadata are queried. A disposable local RSA key signs the RPM; rpmkeys verifies the trusted key, and altered bytes fail. An unsigned RPM can pass digest checking without being authenticated, so `digests OK` alone is rejected as proof of signature. The build and runtime dependency failure paths are deliberately exercised. No `--nodeps` is used to suppress them.

RPM %config(noreplace) preserves administrator edits during upgrade and creates .rpmnew; erasure preserves a modified config as .rpmsave. Debian control declares Depends, conffiles declares persistent configuration, and --force-confold makes the noninteractive preservation choice explicit; the alternative version appears as .dpkg-dist. A failed dpkg install can leave an unpacked package: dependency failure is not an atomic rollback. Removal preserves conffiles; purge removes managed config. User state outside the package file list survives upgrade, rollback and removal. The teaching fixture keeps the same data format in both versions; a real incompatible data migration needs a separate compatibility plan.

A .deb is not intrinsically authenticated by a package checksum. The fixture uses a detached GPG signature over the exact package bytes and verifies that signature with an explicit private public-key ring. Normal Debian repository authentication uses signed repository metadata; this local detached-signature exercise does not claim to implement an APT repository. No maintainer scripts are needed here; if present they require separate review and a confined runtime. Never install an unknown package merely to inspect its contents, and never read host secrets from a build or installation hook.

Rollback here is a native downgrade to the exact earlier package in the same private root, followed by file/config/state checks. It is not a production rollback claim. All disposable package databases, roots, keys, agents and files are removed by the validation harness. Real signing identity, repository trust and production rollout remain outside this exercise.

# Four native query contexts
An RPM file is queried with rpm -qpl FILE; an installed RPM name is queried with rpm --dbpath PRIVATE_DB -ql NAME. Debian package files can be listed with dpkg-deb -c FILE or --fsys-tarfile with a read-only tar reader. Installed Debian package names use dpkg -L NAME or the equivalent dpkg-query --admindir PRIVATE_ROOT/var/lib/dpkg --listfiles NAME. A package name is not a filename, and an uninstalled archive does not require installation to inspect.

The deliverable returns regular-file paths without splitting whitespace inside names. RPM installed paths reflect the explicit relocation prefix; Debian installed package metadata lists original absolute paths and file checks are scoped to the supplied private root. Querying files does not execute maintainer scripts. The checker observes the actual native query child process and verifies the installed package set and payload remain unchanged. It does not accept a fabricated file list or installation followed by deletion as a read-only query.

The four contexts are each executed twice, including package filenames and payload names containing spaces. No global database, host installation or default identity is accessed. The fixture and private databases are removed after validation.
